core.title: Keep plans traceable from train to acceptance test criteria
core.given: You are authoring or changing plan artifacts (trains, wagons, features, WMBTs, acceptances), including acceptance test criteria.
core.when: You create, edit, move or delete any artifact in the hierarchy, its containment links, or an acceptance's test criteria.
core.then: Keep the plan traceable along Train -> Wagon -> Feature -> WMBT -> Acceptance -> Test criteria, each level contained by its parent and guarded by its coverage validators; from Phase 2 (PLANNER_TESTER_ENFORCEMENT) those validators are strict, so their findings block the plan.
prefer: Register each wagon in its train's containment list — the parent kind's containment field, given by the profile's plan-containment idiom (roles.plan_hierarchy#plan_containment).
List each feature in its wagon's containment list (roles.plan_hierarchy#plan_containment).
List each WMBT in its feature's containment list (roles.plan_hierarchy#plan_containment).
Link each WMBT's acceptances through the WMBT's acceptance list (roles.plan_hierarchy#plan_containment) and give each acceptance test criteria.

Before handing off, run the coverage validators along the whole chain of every artifact you changed — its ancestors up to the train and its descendants down to test criteria, not only the level you edited.
Check the project's active rollout phase before deciding whether findings block; if you cannot establish it, report the phase as unknown rather than assuming findings are non-blocking.
avoid: Orphan artifacts that no parent level contains.
Fixing a validator finding by adding placeholder links or empty acceptances instead of real coverage.
core.why: Coverage only means something if every acceptance traces up to a train and down to test criteria; each level is guarded by validators so gaps surface during planning (ATDD Hierarchy Coverage Spec v0.1, section 2), strictly from Phase 2.
evidence: The hierarchy's coverage validators were run along the full chain of every new/changed artifact; in Phase 2 (PLANNER_TESTER_ENFORCEMENT) and later they pass strictly with no findings.
Reviewer can walk each new/changed artifact up to a train and down to acceptance test criteria.
verification: Each level of the plan hierarchy is guarded by its own coverage validators, which check that the level's children are contained by their parent through the parent's containment field (the per-level field names are profile data supplied by roles.plan_hierarchy#plan_containment) and, at the acceptance level, that each acceptance carries test criteria; the concrete validator and finding ids are realization detail.

The validators' disposition is phase-gated and belongs to this rule, not to the profile: before Phase 2 (PLANNER_TESTER_ENFORCEMENT) they are not strict; from Phase 2 onward they are strict and their findings block the plan. Validator behaviour before Phase 2 is unspecified beyond them not being strict.
This rule aggregates the per-level coverage checks of the hierarchy; how a realization splits them into per-level rules is realization detail.
The change facts (containment link changed, acceptance test criteria changed) only target which checks run; they do not narrow scope — the invariant applies to the whole hierarchy.
The check covers only plan artifacts; it does not cover production code or tests that do not touch plan artifacts.
Surfacing validator findings to the planner and determining the active rollout phase need observers beyond what exists today (see activation facts).

values: coverage validator finding of the plan hierarchy

fires: Planner adds a wagon that no train contains
Planner adds a feature that no wagon contains
Planner adds a WMBT that no feature contains, or a WMBT with no acceptances
Planner adds an acceptance not referenced from a WMBT or without test criteria
Planner removes or rewrites the test criteria of an existing acceptance
Planner edits or deletes any train, wagon, feature, WMBT or acceptance
doesNotFire: Edits to production code or tests that do not touch plan artifacts (train, wagon, feature, WMBT, acceptance)

neutralityNotes: The plan-hierarchy level names (train, wagon, feature, WMBT, acceptance) are kept in the core: they are ATDD plan roles that exist in the closed vocabulary (urn artifact types), not stack machinery; each stack's concrete file kinds are supplied by roles.plan_artifact.kinds. Per the round-1 audit, the Phase 2 (PLANNER_TESTER_ENFORCEMENT) strictness threshold is this rule's disposition condition, defined by the ATDD rollout methodology rather than by a stack, so it is kept in the core's then, why, evidence[0], verification and activation.facts[4] — every realization shares the same point at which findings become blocking. The containment field names (participants, features[], wmbts[], acceptances[]) are concrete plan-schema idioms realizing the core's neutral containment links; they are now exposed as profile data through the proposed key roles.plan_hierarchy#plan_containment (no existing key fits), and the core's prefer items, verification and change fact reference that mapping. What remains bunOnly: the per-level validator and finding ids (COVERAGE-PLAN-2.x) — realization detail per notProfileKeys, with core:verification naming the checks generically — and the reference to this stack's related planner.coverage.* rule ids.
